# Command: `i18n` — Translation for Fragments

## Purpose
Make sure translated strings stay correct across htmx swaps — a fragment
returned after a language switch must render in the new language, not
the one the page originally loaded in.

## When to run it
- The audit shows fragment endpoints ignoring the active-language
  session/config value that full-page routes already respect.
- The project needs more than one language and uses htmx-driven partial
  updates.
- User says "the language doesn't update after a swap", "make fragments
  bilingual", or runs `i18n`.
- **Always runs last** — after `fragments`/`swap`/`forms` are stable.

## What it does
1. Every fragment endpoint reads the same active-language value
   (session/config) the backend skill's `i18n.md` already established
   for full pages — never a separate resolution path just for htmx
   routes.
2. Reuse the same `t()`/dictionary helper `i18n.md` set up on the
   backend skill in use — this command does not introduce a second
   translation mechanism.
3. If the project has a language-switcher, switching language should
   itself be an htmx interaction that re-renders the current view's
   fragment in the new language (or does a full boosted navigation if
   simpler) — verify it actually re-renders visible fragments, not just
   the switcher control itself.
4. `dir="rtl"`/`dir="ltr"` lives on the outer `<html>` (set by the
   backend skill's layout) and does not need to change per-fragment —
   verify no fragment template hardcodes a `dir` that could conflict
   with the page's current language.
5. Verify RTL layout still holds after a swap — an OOB swap that injects
   new content can occasionally bypass a stylesheet rule scoped to
   `[dir="rtl"] .some-container`; flag any fragment styling that assumes
   LTR-only spacing.

## Output convention
No new files in the common case — this command wires fragment endpoints
to the existing dictionary/session mechanism from the backend skill.

## Checklist
- [ ] Every fragment endpoint reads the same active-language value as
      full-page routes
- [ ] No second translation/dictionary mechanism introduced
- [ ] Language switcher re-renders visible fragments, not just itself
- [ ] No fragment template hardcodes `dir`
- [ ] RTL verified visually after a swap, not assumed
